name: Folate cycle
summary: Carries one-carbon units. THF picks one up from serine (→ N⁵,N¹⁰-methylene-THF), which either makes thymidine (thymidylate synthase: dUMP → dTMP, leaving DHF that DHFR must reduce back to THF) or is reduced to 5-methyl-THF to remethylate homocysteine (methionine synthase, B12). Drug targets: methotrexate, trimethoprim and pyrimethamine (DHFR); 5-fluorouracil (thymidylate synthase). Folate or B12 deficiency → megaloblastic anemia and ↑ homocysteine; only B12 deficiency also raises methylmalonic acid and causes neurologic signs.

thf.name: Tetrahydrofolate
thf.notes: The active carrier. Dietary folate is reduced to it (via DHF) by DHFR.

mthf.name: N⁵,N¹⁰-Methylene-THF
mthf.notes: The branch point: thymidine synthesis or methyl groups for methionine.

methylthf.name: N⁵-Methyl-THF
methylthf.notes: The main form in blood. Its only way back to THF is methionine synthase, which needs B12: without B12, folate is trapped here (methyl-folate trap).

shmt.name: Serine hydroxymethyltransferase
shmt.notes: Needs B6 (PLP). Serine's side-chain carbon becomes the one-carbon unit; serine becomes glycine.

ts.name: Thymidylate synthase
ts.notes: dUMP → dTMP, the only de novo source of thymidine for DNA. Inhibited by 5-fluorouracil (as FdUMP). Its oxidizing step leaves DHF behind.

dhfr.name: Dihydrofolate reductase
dhfr.notes: Regenerates THF. Inhibited by methotrexate (human), trimethoprim (bacterial) and pyrimethamine (protozoal). Leucovorin (folinic acid) bypasses it, rescuing normal cells from methotrexate.

mthfr.name: Methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase
mthfr.notes: Irreversible: 5-methyl-THF can only return to THF through methionine synthase. Common variant (C677T) → mildly ↑ homocysteine.

ms.name: Methionine synthase
ms.notes: Needs vitamin B12 (methylcobalamin) to carry the methyl group from 5-methyl-THF to homocysteine. B12 deficiency strands folate as 5-methyl-THF (the methyl-folate trap) → megaloblastic anemia, and homocysteine rises. Nitrous oxide inactivates B12 here.
